To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Held-Karp bound is a good approximation to the optimal tour length for most TSP instances, that the expected HK bound can be accurately estimated as a function of the number of cities, that the ratio of optimal tour length to HK bound converges to 1 as N increases, and that the optimal tour length is much smaller than previously believed.

the Held-Karp bound is a good surrogate for the optimal tour, that the ratio of optimal tour length to Held-Karp bound converges to a limit as the instance size increases, and that the limit is less than the commonly cited estimates.

(a) the HK bound is a very accurate approximation to the optimal tour length for both random and real-world instances; (b) the expected HK bound for random Euclidean and random distance matrices can be accurately approximated by a simple formula, and this can be used to estimate the expected optimal tour lengths; and (c) the expected optimal tour for random Euclidean TSP instances is about.7124 times the expected HK bound.
